sermon.title: A man’s portion - June 17, 2024
sermon.speaker: Unidentified speaker (not clearly Pastor Kincer)
sermon.summary: On Father’s Day the message walks through the prodigal son, who wanted only his portion. This life isn’t our whole portion; we create distance from God, waste what we have, and end up serving someone. When the son came to himself and arose, the father ran to him and restored him. Make a full comeback to the Father.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Captions read “prodal/prodical sun”; corrected to prodigal son. The recording places the message first (short, ~19 min) and a worship set after it (~33:25). The slug date (June 17) is the day after Father’s Day 2024.

faqs.question: Is there a sheet?
faqs.answer: Yes, with scriptures to follow along.

faqs.question: Why use the sheet?
faqs.answer: He jokes that hearing his own voice might put him to sleep.

faqs.question: Is our portion just 80 years?
faqs.answer: No; knowing God leads to eternal life.

faqs.question: Is God distant?
faqs.answer: No; He’ll be in your face saying, hey, how you doing?

faqs.question: Is initial belief enough?
faqs.answer: No; you have to keep renewing your relationship with God.

faqs.question: What could the famine be?
faqs.answer: Losing intangible riches: peace, joy, love, a good reputation.

faqs.question: Does God treat us like people do?
faqs.answer: No; the father reestablished his position immediately.

faqs.question: Can I keep one foot in the world?
faqs.answer: Don’t keep your toes in the far country.

faqs.question: Should I just watch the worship?
faqs.answer: No; be a participant with your mouth, posture and hands.
